Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the demo last week. HealthGrid is excited about Redwood and we want to move forward with an annual commitment to cover our inference needs for CareAssist (approx. 8M tokens qtrly). Procurement pushed back on the standard package because of a recent budget realignment.

Short story: we can sign for 1.2M/month (14.4M/year) if you can accommodate a one-time starter credit and a 22% unit-rate adjustment for the first 6 months — otherwise we need to step back to a smaller pilot.

Attached is our internal worksheet for the ask (HealthGrid_MA_Pricing_Sheet_v3.xlsx). We'd like to close this this week. If this needs an exec note, can you route?

— Cory

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Marissa / Jordan — forwarding request from HealthGrid. Deal looks strategic (payer integrations, potential multi-year expansion). They want a temporary 22% unit-rate reduction for 6 months + starter credit to hit their internal FY thresholds.

My read: economics are tight but lifetime value and reference potential are high. Key constraints:
- This would be outside our standard guardrails for mid-market (rate floors + minimum ARR).
- We can probably protect margin by limiting the term of the adjustment (6 months) and ensuring a minimum committed ARR (they're proposing ~$1.2M/month).

Can we get executive exception (VP/CFO) sign-off if we draft a concise memo that:
1) quantifies short-term impact (net revenue delta, margin hit)
2) shows upside (expansion paths, references)
3) includes strict rollback & clawback language

I've attached their sheet and started a memo (Redwood_Exception_Memo_draft.docx). Happy to own the memo drafting — tagging Grace for finance numbers and Jordan for commercial framing.

Naomi
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks for flagging Naomi. Quick thoughts:

1) Commercial: If HealthGrid is committing to 14.4M tokens/year (1.2M/month) that's meaningful. Jordan, confirm net-new ARR profile and typical churn assumptions for this cohort.

2) Finance: I will need a conservative P&L view for the 6-month concession window and a 24-month projection showing payback. Grace — can you produce:
   - Estimated token-unit margin change at the proposed 22% discount
   - Dollar impact of starter credit (we should cap it)
   - Proposed clawback schedule tied to attainment

3) Risk controls: Any exception must include:
   - Auto-revert to standard pricing after 6 months
   - Minimum annualized commit or prepayment milestone
   - Legal to vet language around credits & refunds

If the numbers look tolerable, I will sign off and take it to CFO for final approval. Please prioritize the memo; Naomi, can you get HealthGrid to agree verbally to the rollback & clawback? We need that in writing before CFO review.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Operations

Adding commercial math to inform the memo — roughs below.

HealthGrid ask: 22% discount on unit rate for 6 months + $75k starter credit (they flagged that as the ask in the sheet).

Assumptions (rounded):
- Committed tokens: 1.2M tokens/month -> 14.4M/year
- Standard unit price (list): $0.0035 per token
- Proposed discounted unit price: $0.00273 per token (22% off)

6-month revenue at discounted rate (tokens billed monthly at committed volume):
= 1.2M * 6 * $0.00273 = $19,656
Standard revenue at list for same period:
= 1.2M * 6 * $0.0035 = $25,200
Gross revenue delta over 6 months: ~$5.5k (this seems small because example unit prices are illustrative; confirm true unit economics with finance)

Starter credit: $75k one-time — this is material vs 6-month billing; we should cap starter credits to no more than X% of first-yr ARR.

Note: The real margin impact depends heavily on inference unit cost (GPU ops), caching, and their actual token consumption distribution. Grace, please firm up cost per token and net margin.

If finance can show payback within 9–12 months with clear expansion triggers, I support moving to CFO for sign-off with strict rollback.

— Jordan
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts

Thanks team — I ran the numbers and updated the attached exception memo. Highlights below (to put into a one-pager for CFO):

- 6-month concession: discounted revenue delta = -$5,470 (as Jordan calculated with illustrative list price).
- Starter credit: I recommend capping at $25k (instead of their requested $75k) and structuring it as a credit applied across the first 3 invoice cycles to reduce churn risk.
- Margin impact: using our operational cost model (includes batching & KV caching assumptions) the net margin reduction over the 6-month window is ~12 percentage points; payback expected in month 10 if expansion assumptions hold (50% likelihood).
- Controls proposed:
  * Automatic reversion to standard prices after 6 months
  * Clawback: credits prorated and recouped if monthly committed usage falls below 80% of the agreed commit in months 4–6
  * Legal to review credit/clawback text before signature

Ask for CFO: approval to (a) accept a temporary 22% unit-rate adjustment for 6 months, (b) authorize a capped starter credit of $25k, and (c) approve the attached memo language for contract amendment.

I've attached: Redwood_Exception_Memo_draft.docx (with numbers and proposed contract language) and updated the HealthGrid_MA_Pricing_Sheet_v3.xlsx with modeled scenarios.

Marissa — if you sign this, I'll route to CFO (I'll include the one-pager and the scenario appendix). Naomi — please confirm HealthGrid verbally accepts the rollback & clawback structure before I route.

Grace O'Connor
Finance Lead, Commercial Finance
